newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan president names ally as Punjab governor.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan president names ally as Punjab governor.

text.p: Pakistan President Farooq Leghari named a close confidant as governor of Punjab on Monday in an apparent power-sharing in the most populous province with new Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's ruling party.

The appointment of Shahid Hamid, a lawyer who was defence minister in a recent caretaker government, also partly broke a stalemate in the formation of cabinets in three of Pakistan's four provinces five weeks after Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League (PML) won a landslide victory in February 3 elections.

The appointment was announced soon after sitting governor Ahmad Tariq Rahim swore in a 10-member Punjab cabinet and then resigned, threatening to make disclosures about critics of his conduct during his four months in office.
Cabinets in Punjab as well as in Sindh and North West Frontier provinces had been held up by differences between Sharif and Leghari over new governors or ministers, political sources said.
Punjab chief minister Shahbaz Sharif, younger brother of the prime minister, announced his cabinet on Monday after a conciliation meeting last week with Leghari.
PML chief ministers in Sindh and the Frontier have yet to name their cabinets, while the PML has not implemented its gubernatorial or ministerial pledges with coalition partners.
Pakistan's constitution gives the president power to appoint a governor in consultation with the prime minister.
Rahim said in a letter to Leghari on Monday he was resigning as Punjab governor because the PML had found it difficult to have a working relationship with him.
"This is surprising in view of the fact that the PML leadership articulated no such qualms during the interim period of the caretaker regime," he said.
He was referring to a caretaker government Leghari had set up to oversee elections after he sacked former prime minister Benazir Bhutto on November 5 on disputed charges of misrule.

Rahim, a former member of Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party and named governor on November 5 as part of the interim set-up, has been accused by the PML of having tried unsucessfully to debar some party leaders from elections.
Rahim denied this and said his oath of office prevented him commenting on or revealing certain facts.

"But there may be time in the future when I might have to consider sifting information...in order to expose the motives of some of those who have proclaimed themselves to be the champions of free elections, fair play and democracy," he said.
Bhutto accuses the caretakers of rigging the February 3 elections, in which she suffered a crushing defeat. The government denies the charge.
